reasoning_trace.description: MANDATORY: You MUST describe what you see in the images (Charts, System Models) to prove you have analyzed them.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures and charts, including system diagrams, block diagrams, hardware photos, and performance curves. Figure 3 shows the system diagram and signal processing, including the geometry, transmitted OFDM signal, and returned signals from two tags with OOK modulation. Figure 4 illustrates the block diagram of the receiver and the SIC framework. Other figures show the LED board design, thermal management, experimental setup, and performance curves for retro-reflected power vs lateral distance.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The system uses a hybrid MRR-assisted long-range SDMA for RO-ISAC systems. The ISAC coupling mode is based on a hybrid retro-reflector architecture, which combines a stable, unmodulated retro-reflector (URR) for high-precision ranging with a modulated retro-reflector (MRR) for embedding a unique ID via on-off keying (OOK). The system also employs a successive interference cancellation (SIC) framework to resolve the near-far problem and separate the signals from multiple tags.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports a ranging accuracy of centimeter-level at a 5-meter range, with a communication uplink of several hundred hertz per tag at a bit-error rate below 10^-3. The system's performance is validated through high-fidelity simulations parameterized by experimental data from a custom-built, high-power optical testbed. The results show that the system can achieve simultaneous ranging and communication for two concurrent tags, with a ranging accuracy of 95% within a centimeter-level range.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper solves the problem of achieving long-range SDMA in RO-ISAC systems using a hybrid MRR-assisted architecture and SIC framework. However, the system still faces challenges such as the limited modulation bandwidth of the light source, which affects the multi-tag positioning accuracy and uplink concurrency. Future work will focus on developing an integrated hardware transceiver for real-time operation, designing more robust channel estimation and SIC algorithms to support larger tag populations, and extending the system from one-dimensional ranging to two-dimensional positioning.
